statement: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$. Point $D$ lies on side $\overline{BC}$ so that $AD = DC$. The measure of angle $BAD$ is twice the measure of angle $ABC$. What is the measure of angle $BAD$, in degrees?

choices.misconception: I solved for the base angle, $x = 36$, and gave it as the answer instead of angle $BAD = 2x$.
I treated angle $BAD = 2x$ as the whole angle at $A$, so I wrote $2x + x + x = 180$, got $x = 45$ and angle $BAD = 90$.
I set up $5x = 180$ correctly but gave the whole angle $BAC = 3x = 108$ instead of angle $BAD$.

hints: Call angle $ABC$ $x$. Two different isosceles triangles give you equal angles.
$AB = AC$ makes angle $ACB = x$. $AD = DC$ makes triangle $ADC$ isosceles, so angle $DAC$ equals angle $DCA = x$ too.
Angle $BAC = $ angle $BAD + $ angle $DAC = 2x + x = 3x$. The angle sum in triangle $ABC$ is $3x + x + x = 180$.

solutions.reliable: Let angle $ABC = x$. Since $AB = AC$, angle $ACB = x$. Since $AD = DC$, triangle $ADC$ is isosceles with equal base angles at $A$ and $C$, so angle $DAC = x$. Then angle $BAC = $ angle $BAD + $ angle $DAC = 2x + x = 3x$. In triangle $ABC$: $3x + x + x = 180$, so $x = 36$ and angle $BAD = 2x = 72$ degrees. Check: triangle $ABD$ has angles $72^\circ$ at $A$, $36^\circ$ at $B$ and $72^\circ$ at $D$, which add to $180^\circ$, and triangle $ADC$ has angles $36^\circ$, $36^\circ$ and $108^\circ$.
